runs.text: Unexpected inflation redistributes purchasing power between borrowers and lenders on fixed nominal contracts. Even expected inflation can create costs: changing posted prices uses resources (menu costs), economizing on cash takes time and effort (shoeleather costs), and uneven price changes can obscure relative-price signals.

transcript.sourceText: A lender makes a 9% loan expecting 3% inflation, so the expected real return is approximately 6%. Actual inflation turns out to be 10%, making the realized real return approximately 9% - 10% = -1%. Unexpected inflation transfers purchasing power from the lender to the borrower.
transcript.text: A lender makes a 9 percent loan expecting 3 percent inflation, so the expected real return is approximately 6 percent . Actual inflation turns out to be 10 percent , making the realized real return approximately 9 percent minus 10 percent equals -1 percent . Unexpected inflation transfers purchasing power from the lender to the borrower.

rawReadingSequence: Outcome: Analyze redistribution, shoeleather costs, menu costs, and price distortions.

Unexpected inflation redistributes purchasing power between borrowers and lenders on fixed nominal contracts. Even expected inflation can create costs: changing posted prices uses resources (menu costs), economizing on cash takes time and effort (shoeleather costs), and uneven price changes can obscure relative-price signals.
Unexpected inflation lowers the real repayment on a fixed nominal debt.
Menu costs are resources spent changing posted prices.
Shoeleather costs arise from efforts to hold less money during inflation.
Relative-price confusion can make economic decisions harder.
Do not confuse shoeleather costs with menu costs. Shoeleather costs are the wasted effort people spend trying to hold less money during inflation.

A lender makes a 9% loan expecting 3% inflation, so the expected real return is approximately 6%. Actual inflation turns out to be 10%, making the realized real return approximately 9% - 10% = -1%. Unexpected inflation transfers purchasing power from the lender to the borrower.
